recipes.name: Ingrid's Caesar Salad Dressing
ingredients_raw: 2 dashes hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®)

steps.text: Beat together mayonnaise, olive oil, Parmesan cheese, blue cheese dressing, vinegar, garlic, lemon juice, dry mustard, Worcestershire sauce, hot pepper sauce, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper, and anchovy paste in a bowl until well blended.
Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Ingrid's Caesar Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This inspired version of a Caesar salad dressing is bursting with flavor. Garlic, mustard powder, hot sauce, and cayenne give this dressing a unique zip.

review.reviewBody: I wish I could give this more than 5 stars. It's delicious. Here's a response to the poster who gave only 1 star because of the recipe's name, even though he admitted that it was tasty. First of all, the recipe is NOT named "Classic Caesar Salad Dressing" - it's named "Ingrid's Caesar Salad Dressing". Because it bears Ingrid's name, she has the right to adjust the ingredients list to her liking. Emeril does it, Bobby Flay does it, etc. What would be the point of this website if everyone used exactly the same ingredients for every recipe? BORING!! Kudos to MommyKirsten for having the heart of an artist and the palate of a chef and for sharing her recipe. If you agree, give it a thumbs-up.
Used 1 can of anchovies, 1/2 c grated Parmesan, increased lemon juice to about 2 or 3 tbsp (to taste), and nixed the cayenne for my sensitive hubby. Turned out delish!
really good. i had to make some changes but what a wonderful base. i like it much more tangier so i doubled the vinegar, 4x the mustard, and doubled the hot sauce.

Since I have to rate this to offer comment, I will give it a 5. With that said, I didn't follow it. I eye-balled the measurements, substituted anchovies for fish sauce, garlic juice vice pureed garlic, blue cheese blended with heavy cream and some leftover juice from some filling for a stuffed avocado. Added in more fish sauce and Worcestershire. It still turned out great. Even my wife liked it. If anything, the combo of ingredients works and it's forgiving on the measurements. Lots of room to be creative and still end up with a wonderful result.

I was so pleased with this recipe, it was the best Ceaser dressing I have ever had. I had no anchovy paste so I substituted with two canned anchovies and it blew my mind! Thank you so much for this recipe, everyone raved about it including my son in law who generally has to have his mouth pried open to eat a salad, he even asked for the recipe...lol.
very flavorful! I didnt have the bleu cheese dressing but it's great without it.

Cannot buy caesar dressing where I live so this is a good substitute. Do not sell anchovy paste here either so I used about a teaspoon of Thai fish sauce instead.
Mine was a little too thick to pour so I thinned it with milk to the consistency I wanted.

Okay, so I hate it when people change everything about a recipe and then rate it. That being said, I had a lime instead of a lemon and I had no blue cheese anything so didn’t include that or the anchovies. It was still delicious so I’m going to go out on a limb here and say that this recipe, as written, would also be delicious.
Been using this for years...fantastic...one in a wee while I add a tsp of honey..more for me. But usually nothing is changed.
Better than anything you can buy in the store. Used it for years. I use half the Mayo and double the olive oil. I would like other recipes from this chef.

I have been making this every week for months (years maybe). Caesar salad is my family’s fav and this dressing rocks. I do add the anchovy paste. The only change is that I just add 2T blue cheese crumbles in place of the dressing. So so good. Thanks for the recipe!!
Followed the recipe, except used pecorino romano, and it's fantasic!

I made this as is. It was worth the effort to hunt down the ingredients. My entire table was delighted with the results even though I served it immediately. I was happy to have saved $10 on the store-bought bottle of Cardini's that I otherwise would have bought. Thank you for posting this recipe.

This is fantastic! If course we use it on Ceasar salad, but also as a spread on club house sandwiches, veggie dip and pizza crust dip. It's pretty good as a base for chicken salad sandwiches / salad. I can see myself finding many more uses for this recipe... Like to coat chicken?.... 🤔
Yummy! Love the bit of heat!
This is the second time I’ve made this dressing and it’s SOOO much better than store bought ❤️ Thank you for a great recipe
Make it all the time and love it!
So delicious! Even better than most restaurants! I will never buy store-bought dressing again. This was easy to make and has amazing flavor.

I made this once to bring to a party and ever since, I haven’t bought salad dressing because this is so easy and so good. It’s kind of a cross between Caesar, blue cheese and creamy garlic. I make it exactly as written, and serve with mixed spring greens, thinly sliced red onion, shaved Parmesan, and other salad veggies. Perfection!
I've been using this recipe for years (really), and my family loves it! Big thank you to Ingrid for sharing her yummy recipe!
